texts.bulletin: Harvest disruption risk in Buguey due to rainfall of 38.3 mm/24h. texts.bulletin: DANGER — Extreme rainfall recorded in Claveria, Cagayan (100.6 mm/24h). Suspend ALL field operations. Avoid crossing rivers and flood-prone areas. texts.sms: DA ALERT: Extreme rain in Claveria. Suspend all farm work. Secure produce. Contact MAO for assistance.
texts.lgu:
AGRICULTURAL EMERGENCY ADVISORY — Claveria
Extreme rainfall (100.6 mm/24h) requires immediate action:
1. Advise farmers to suspend all field operations immediately.
2. Coordinate with MDRRMC for damage assessment teams.
3. Pre-position tarpaulins and drying facilities.
4. Activate emergency seed replacement protocols.
5. Document affected crop areas for PCIC crop insurance filing.

texts.bulletin: Harvest disruption risk in Gonzaga due to rainfall of 25.4 mm/24h. Farmers in ripening or harvesting stages should: (1) Defer combine harvester deployment to avoid bogging; (2) Protect cut stalks from further wetting; (3) Prioritize mechanical drying over sun-drying for collected grain. Postharvest drying risk is ELEVATED. Coordinate with DA mechanization service providers for mobile dryer access.
texts.sms: DA ADVISORY: Rain risk for harvest in Gonzaga. Defer harvest, use mechanical dryer if available. Call MAO for help.
texts.lgu:
HARVEST ADVISORY — Gonzaga
Rainfall of 25.4 mm may disrupt ongoing harvest operations.
Recommended actions:
1. Advise farmers to assess field conditions before deploying machinery.
2. Coordinate with RCEF mechanization pool for mobile dryer deployment.
3. Issue tarpaulin assistance where needed.
4. Document areas where harvest was deferred for scheduling follow-up.

📞 Contact your Municipal Agriculturist for drying support.

texts.bulletin: OPERATIONS ADVISORY - DEFER OPEN-AIR GRAIN DRYING - Cordon: sun-drying of palay or corn grain should be deferred. Basis: high humidity slows drying and increases mold or grain-quality risk. ACAP calendar anchor: Aug 16-31 - Rice season 2 - Reproductive; Corn season 2 - Reproductive. Recommended action: avoid open sun-drying; use covered temporary storage or mechanical drying where available.

texts.bulletin: Harvest disruption risk in Dupax del Norte due to rainfall of 23.7 mm/24h. Farmers in ripening or harvesting stages should: (1) Defer combine harvester deployment to avoid bogging; (2) Protect cut stalks from further wetting; (3) Prioritize mechanical drying over sun-drying for collected grain. Postharvest drying risk is ELEVATED. Coordinate with DA mechanization service providers for mobile dryer access.

HARVEST ADVISORY — Dupax del Norte
Rainfall of 23.7 mm may disrupt ongoing harvest operations.
Recommended actions:
1. Advise farmers to assess field conditions before deploying machinery.
2. Coordinate with RCEF mechanization pool for mobile dryer deployment.
3. Issue tarpaulin assistance where needed.
4. Document areas where harvest was deferred for scheduling follow-up.

texts.bulletin: Harvest disruption risk in Santa Fe due to rainfall of 35.8 mm/24h. Farmers in ripening or harvesting stages should: (1) Defer combine harvester deployment to avoid bogging; (2) Protect cut stalks from further wetting; (3) Prioritize mechanical drying over sun-drying for collected grain. Postharvest drying risk is ELEVATED. Coordinate with DA mechanization service providers for mobile dryer access.
texts.sms: DA ADVISORY: Rain risk for harvest in Santa Fe. Defer harvest, use mechanical dryer if available. Call MAO for help.
texts.lgu:
HARVEST ADVISORY — Santa Fe
Rainfall of 35.8 mm may disrupt ongoing harvest operations.
Recommended actions:
1. Advise farmers to assess field conditions before deploying machinery.
2. Coordinate with RCEF mechanization pool for mobile dryer deployment.
3. Issue tarpaulin assistance where needed.
4. Document areas where harvest was deferred for scheduling follow-up.

📞 Contact your Municipal Agriculturist for drying support.
